title: Google Tests Gemini's Direct Purchase Function on Flipkart, AI In-App Checkout to Launch Soon

content_html:
Google is accelerating the deployment of large models in e-commerce transactions. Recently, Google launched an early test in the Indian market, allowing some users to directly purchase products from Walmart's e-commerce platform Flipkart through Gemini and AI modes. This move marks that Google's artificial intelligence services are moving beyond mere product recommendations and information retrieval, officially extending into the commercial transaction loop.

In the current testing experience, when users search for selected products such as smartphones, electronics, and phone accessories, a "Buy" button appears in the AI interface's Flipkart product list. Clicking it allows direct access to Flipkart's brand checkout process without leaving the current AI interface.

The underlying technology behind this feature can be traced back to Google's Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP), launched earlier this year. This open standard aims to enable seamless interaction between AI agents and retailers throughout the entire shopping lifecycle, including the checkout process. Currently, this direct purchasing test is only available to a small number of users and specific categories. Although competitors' products such as Amazon are also displayed on the same platform, they are not yet integrated with this one-click purchasing option.

This collaboration not only reflects deep technological coordination but also confirms their solid capital connection — Google invested about $350 million in 2024 to acquire a minority stake in Flipkart. According to insiders, Google plans to widely promote this commercial experience before the Indian holiday shopping season in late October.

As leading manufacturers like OpenAI continue to invest in the commercial functions of AI products, large models are rapidly evolving into intelligent agents that drive actual transactions. This will not only intensify competition in India's e-commerce market, which has over a billion internet users, but may also profoundly reshape the global online retail landscape.
